title: Snakes and Ladders
statement_short: Given an n x n board where squares are labeled 1 to n^2 in a Boustrophedon style, find the minimum number of moves to reach square n^2\. Some squares contain snakes or ladders that destination-jump players upon landing.
constraints: 2 <= n <= 20, board[i][j] is -1 or between 1 and n^2
hint: Small board dimension (n <= 20) allows unweighted shortest path search from square 1 to n^2 using queue traversal.
why_not: Right: Graph BFS finds the shortest path on an unweighted game board grid in O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space. Not 1D DP: Board moves contain snakes that create backward edges (cycles), causing infinite loops in standard DP. Not Backtracking: Exploring all dice roll sequences causes exponential TLE. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Priority queues add O(log N) overhead when edge weights are all uniformly equal to 1.
